final_candidates.decision_summary: Highest EVEscape score (0.705) and highest evolutionary tolerance (0.158) among all candidates. Lysine disrupts the N-X-T glycosylation motif while maintaining a polar residue at the surface.
Second-highest EVEscape score (0.687) with strong escape signal. Low evolutionary tolerance (0.013) is a concern but the large basic residue effectively abolishes the glycan attachment site.
Third-highest EVEscape (0.627) with moderate evolutionary tolerance (0.026). Aspartate is a known glycan-loss escape pathway in HIV-1 Env, removing the N-linked glycan acceptor.

stop_reason.detail: All 4 available tool calls have been used; evidence is sufficient to finalize the top-3 ranking.

history.rationale: N301 is a conserved glycan at the base of the V3 loop involved in binding by multiple bnAbs including 2G12 and PGT128-class antibodies. Loss of this glycan is a known escape route with moderate fitness cost.
Lowest EVEscape score (0.558) among retained candidates with low MSA frequency (0.039). A is a minimal side-chain substitution that removes glycosylation.
Lowest-tier escape score (0.558) with very low evolutionary tolerance (0.039) and zero PLM. Alanine removes the glycan but provides minimal escape advantage.

rejection.reason: Lowest-tier escape score (0.558) with very low evolutionary tolerance (0.039) and zero PLM. Alanine removes the glycan but provides minimal escape advantage.
